package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript that attempts to disable Windows Defender, a clear sign of malicious intent. This behavior is not expected from any legitimate npm package and poses a direct threat to system security.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the package is executed or imported)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file (index.js or similar entry point)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code spawns a child process to execute a PowerShell command that disables Windows Defender's real-time monitoring, reducing system defenses.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling antivirus or endpoint protection is a classic malware tactic to evade detection and facilitate further malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not attempt to alter system security settings or disable antivirus software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administration tools may disable Defender as part of a managed security policy, but never from a general-purpose npm package.
key_indicators: Use of child_process to run system-level commands
Direct attempt to disable Windows Defender

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed and executed, triggering obfuscated code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Disables Windows Defender, reducing system security and enabling further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Use of child_process or exec to run system commands
Attempts to disable antivirus or endpoint protection
file_indicators: index.js or main entry file containing obfuscated code
References to Set-MpPreference or PowerShell commands in package files
network_indicators: None observed in this specific sample, but further analysis may reveal C2 or exfiltration attempts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan npm packages for obfuscated JavaScript, especially code that invokes child_process or attempts to run PowerShell commands related to system security settings. Flag any package that tries to disable Windows Defender or other endpoint protection as highly suspicious.
